item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"medium","summary":"A is narrowly preferable because its out-of-contract retry change is limited to seekable bodies, whereas B globally buffers nearly every non-standard reader. Neither patch is merge-ready because both bypass FilesService.Add instead of routing Upload through it.","reasons":["Both Upload implementations correctly validate inputs, use multipartbody.NewFile with field \"file\", and return decoded File data.","Both violate the explicit reuse requirement by duplicating Add's option handling, Raw.Do call, response decoding, and missing-data check instead of calling s.Add(ctx, body, contentType, opts...).","A's retry test verifies that the multipart file content survives the 429 retry; B's Upload retry test only drains the body and does not verify the replayed multipart name, filename, or content.","A's RawClient change is unnecessary and prohibited by the contract, but it is narrower than B's global buffering of all unrecognized readers, including non-seekable streams and requests that may not actually be retried."],"risks_a":["enableBodyReplay's GetBody returns another wrapper around the same mutable seeker rather than a new independent body, contrary to net/http's new-copy expectation and potentially unsafe if attempts overlap.","It changes RawClient and caller-owned closer semantics despite the contract forbidding unrelated retry refactoring.","It lacks the required Upload-level source-reader failure test."],"risks_b":["replayableReader fully consumes every unrecognized reader unless WithNoRetry is present, introducing broad memory, latency, blocking-stream, and error-timing changes outside file uploads.","Buffering is triggered without checking whether the configured policy and HTTP method can actually retry.","Upload duplicates Add rather than preserving one path for options and error semantics, and its retry test does not validate the multipart payload on the second attempt."]}
